title: PR lifecycle notes - code reflect notebook (HAO)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal notebook for the recent PR (ref: GH #842). Mixing rapid notes, a short checklist I use when triaging multi-file PRs, and a few low-effort follow-ups to catch later. Not intended to be polished; copy useful bits into PR comments or a GH review as needed.

Context summary (TL;DR):
- PR changes split KV-cache eviction logic and introduces a new eviction policy selector. Affects kv_cache_manager.*, serving loop, and a handful of unit tests.
- Motivation: reduce tail latency for long-sequence streaming by avoiding full-cache copies on small writes.
- Risk areas: concurrency in eviction, serialized snapshot format bump (on-disk), and interaction with quantized model runtimes (cache keys include tensor dtype metadata).

Local repro steps (quick):
- checkout branch: git fetch origin && git checkout pr/842-eviction-selector
- run failing test locally: pytest tests/kv_cache/test_eviction.py::TestSelector::test_concurrent_eviction -k slow
- reproduce perf regression: python tools/bench_kvcache.py --seq 2048 --iters 500 --w=32
- run a single CPU race check (sanity): PYTHONASYNCIODEBUG=1 pytest -q tests/ -k eviction -q

Initial observations after running tests:
- Two intermittent failures seen locally: one is assertion on snapshot version mismatch, another is a flaky timing-dependent failure in TestSelector (order of callbacks).
- Bench shows ~6% lower throughput on short sequences (seq < 256) when the selector path takes the policy switch. Need to confirm if selector adds branching overhead; suspect allocation pattern.

Reviewer quick checklist (copyable snippets):
- Safety/semantics:
  - [ ] Does new selector change public API or on-disk snapshot format? (yes -> bump version + migration path)
  - [ ] Are data races prevented when eviction triggers during an ongoing write? Look for lock-free patterns and double-checked locking pitfalls.
  - [ ] Are invariants asserted in debug builds, and are those asserts covered by tests?
- Tests/coverage:
  - [ ] Unit tests for each policy code path (LRU, TTL, size-based, random fallback).
  - [ ] Regression test for snapshot compatibility (old snapshots -> new code).
  - [ ] Add a deterministic concurrency harness test (thread interleave simulation).
- Performance:
  - [ ] Microbench every code path (selector fast path vs fallback).
  - [ ] Check object allocations/GC during fast path (py-spy / tracemalloc).
- Observability:
  - [ ] Add short metrics: selector_selection_count, selector_latency_ms (p95/p99), selector_switch_rate.
  - [ ] Ensure new log lines are structured (json) and include correlation id for request.
- Migration and rollout strategy:
  - [ ] Canary rollout on Dedicated pools with low traffic (select subset of users).
  - [ ] Auto-fallback if selector latency > baseline by 15% for 5m.

Concrete nit / code notes to leave in review comments:
- kv_cache_manager/select.py: prefer early return to nested if/else here; reduces branch mispredicts.
- Avoid allocating a new tuple for key metadata on the hot path; reuse a preallocated lightweight struct if possible.
- Inline small selector helper (single-use) to avoid call overhead in the hot path.
- Snapshot version bump must be accompanied by a comment explaining compatibility semantics (why the bump, what fields changed).

Refactor ideas (medium-term):
- Extract a Selectors registry (dict[str->callable]) with a minimal interface: pick(request_meta)->policy. Allows O(1) lookup without concrete policy branching tree.
- Move policy decision to router-level in serving loop (higher level) so multiple cache managers share same decision, avoiding duplicated logic.
- Consider a thin C-extension / cython hot path for selector when we see repeated keys to reduce Python call overhead. Add feature flag behind runtime param.

Low-effort follow-ups (create tickets):
- Add metric: evictions_per_minute_by_policy (small ticket, low risk).
- Add deterministic concurrency harness for eviction (JIRA-ENG-1276 was created for this).
- Small README docs for snapshot versioning (where to look, migration steps).
- Add integration test that writes snapshot, restarts service, reads snapshot back and validates KV consistency.

Suggested test cases to add (copyable):
1) test_snapshot_backward_compat: write v1 snapshot, start New code, ensure load succeeds and contents identical
2) test_selector_does_not_block_writer: spawn writer thread + eviction thread -> assert writer latency < threshold
3) test_policy_switch_perf: compare walltime for 10k selector invocations across branches (assert < baseline * 1.05)

Small pseudo-diff suggestions (for quick fixes):
- In select.py: replace
  if cond_a:
      if cond_b:
          do_x()
      else:
          do_y()
  with
  if cond_a and cond_b:
      do_x()
  elif cond_a:
      do_y()

- Avoid constructing key_meta = (dtype, shape, seq) on each request; instead: key_meta = key_meta_pool.get_or_create(dtype, shape)

Open questions / TODOs (need answers from author):
- Was the snapshot version bump intentional or an accidental side effect of adding a field?
- Any constraints from the runtime team re: on-disk footprint increase? (Diego to weigh in)
- Are there customers who rely on exact snapshot binary format? We need to check SRE/CS tracker.

Rollout checklist (Ops):
- Deploy behind feature flag called kvcache.selector.v2=false by default
- Canary on dedicated-capacity pool id: dc-small-3 for 6 hours
- Monitor selector_latency_ms (p99), eviction_rate, and error_rate per-pool
- If p99 selector latency > baseline * 1.15 -> disable flag automatically and roll back

Estimated effort and priority: 
- Small fixes and metrics: 2 days (add metrics + small code tidy)
- Tests and concurrency harness: 4-6 days
- Migration docs + snapshot compatibility: 1 day
- Total (to be safe): 1 sprint (roughly 2 weeks)

Personal next steps (for me):
- [ ] Leave inline GH comments for obvious nits (small diffs).
- [ ] Run full benchmark suite and post numbers in PR comment.
- [ ] Draft a short canary playbook and share with SRE on Slack (#sre-evictions).
- [ ] File follow-up tickets for metrics and docs.

Slack references / context: #serving-runtime thread 2025-02-13 09:17AM (see linked GH PR for thread link).

Quick copy snippets for PR comment: (pick one or two)
- "Nice extraction overall — a few concurrency edge-cases around the selector path need guardrails. I left inline notes + a suggested deterministic harness test. Also recommend adding selector metrics before rolling this out to Dedicated."
- "We should gate this behind a feature flag and do a short canary run. I'll prepare the canary config if you want me to."

-- end --

Notes to self: keep this doc short-lived. After PR merges, move the checklist bits into an internal checklist template under eng docs and close any small tickets created above.
